To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. The evolution of a norm is not necessarily a smooth process; 2. Norms are more likely to evolve successfully when participants have a shared sense of identity and a sense of community; 3. The online environment can be designed to facilitate the development of norms

the evolution of norms in a newly forming group is influenced by the design of the online environment and that visibility of participants is one important factor that contributes towards the evolution of norms.

(1) a design that promotes visibility of all participants can be used to overcome the forces for dissolution of a group; and (2) the evolution of norms is an important part of a group’s development, and a group that fails to evolve norms successfully will likely dissolve.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of norms in a newly forming online group.
how people in a group develop a sense of community and a sense of identity.
how to design environments that support the evolution of shared norms and identities in newly forming groups.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the evolution of norms in newly forming groups is not a simple process and requires careful consideration of the design of an online space that supports the visibility and participation of all members of the group.

the design of the online environment and the way the group members interact with it, are both important for the evolution of norms in a newly forming group, as well as the evolution of a group identity.
the evolution of norms in a newly forming group is an ongoing and dynamic process that is affected by the design of the online environment and the actions of the group members.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that it is possible to design a system to support a newly forming group in the evolution of its norms, and that such a system can help to overcome forces that would otherwise lead to the dissolution of the group.
the evolution of norms in a newly forming group is facilitated when participants are made aware of each other’s actions and reactions.

we have demonstrated that a group of strangers with no prior relationship can successfully form a community of practice, even in an online environment, if the group is provided a mechanism for making its norms transparent to all participants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to create a design environment that enables people to discuss norms and to resolve disagreements about them.
the design of online spaces for group formation and interaction should promote the visibility of participants and the visibility of norms.
the evolution of norms can be facilitated through a design that promotes visibility and accountability of participants.
